extracted.intended_audience: NEH staff, grant recipients, auditors, state humanities councils, and members of the public (potential whistleblowers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the NEH Office of Inspector General's responsibilities, authorities, reporting channels for alleged waste/fraud/mismanagement, and the audit-related forms/guidelines and peer-review resources available to grant recipients and oversight professionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Inspector General responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Inspector General is responsible for (1) conducting audits and investigations; (2) reviewing legislation; (3) recommending policies to promote efficiency and effectiveness; and (4) preventing and detecting fraud, waste, and abuse in the operations of the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Inspector General is also responsible for keeping the NEH chairman and Congress informed of problems or deficiencies in NEH’s programs and operations. (Original wording preserved.)

rubrics_metrics.name: OIG independence and statutory authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The law gives the IG the power to act independently: the IG cannot be prevented from initiating, carrying out, or completing an audit or investigation, or from issuing any subpoena; has access to all records of the agency; reports directly to Congress; and can only be removed by the National Council on the Humanities, who must promptly advise Congress of the reasons for the removal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes the OIG's authority to access records, issue subpoenas, and report independently to Congress — key procedural and legal protections that affect audit scope and enforceability.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to report waste, fraud, and mismanagement (contact channels)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are four ways to contact NEH’s OIG to report an act you believe to be wasteful or fraudulent: CALL (toll-free): 1 (877) 786-7598; WRITE: Office of Inspector General, National Endowment for the Humanities, 400 7th Street, SW, Washington, DC 20506; EMAIL: [email]; INTERNET FORM: click here. Fraud can also be reported using the General Accounting Office’s Fraudnet Web site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide allegations via phone, mail, email, or online form. The page lists specific contact points and points users to GAO Fraudnet as an alternative reporting channel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of reportable allegations / misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: You can provide information about allegations or suspicions of waste, fraud, abuse, mismanagement, research misconduct (fabrication, falsification, plagiarism), or unnecessary government expenditures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly enumerates categories of misconduct to report, including research misconduct subtypes; reporters should frame allegations within these categories when contacting OIG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whistleblower protections and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Government employees are protected from reprisal. Your identity will [be] held in confidence, unless the Inspector General determines the disclosure to be unavoidable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters (including government employees) are informed of non‑reprisal protections and that their identity will be kept confidential except when disclosure is unavoidable; this affects what information reporters may provide and expectations about privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: External peer review of the NEH OIG audit organization (audit quality transparency)
rubrics_metrics.description: OIG Peer Review Reports: External Review of the NEH OIG Audit Organization — reports listed for September 2022, August 2019, December 2016, September 2013, December 2010, and September 2007 (PDFs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presence and dates of periodic external peer reviews indicate an audit quality oversight practice; reviewers or recipients can consult these reports to assess OIG audit performance and compliance with professional audit standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program‑specific audit guides and accounting/manual templates (required/expected documentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms and Guidelines listed: Program-Specific Audit Guide: Federal/State Partnership Program [CFDA No. 45.129]; Accounting System Manual for State Humanities Councils, revised January 2009; Sample Personnel Activity Report; Program-Specific Audit Guide for Recipients of NEH Challenge Grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These documents are cited as resources that define audit expectations, required accounting practices, and sample documentation (e.g., personnel activity reports) for NEH grant recipients and state councils; users should consult the specific guides for detailed compliance requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional grant oversight and fraud-prevention resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Other Resources: NEH Research Misconduct Policy; Fraudnet; IGNet (website of the Federal Inspector General community); A Guide to Grant Oversight and Best Practices for Combating Grant Fraud (National Procurement Fraud Task Force); Message from the National Procurement Fraud Task Force; Improving the Grant Management Process (U.S. Department of Justice Office of the Inspector General, February 2009).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These external documents and resources provide supplemental best practices, policies, and guidance on oversight, grant management improvements, and anti‑fraud measures that grant managers and auditors should consult to align with federal best practices.
